summary: The manufacturer behind cars sold through ARENA and NEXA, with parts, servicing-related offerings and exports.
description: Maruti Suzuki India designs or develops vehicles, arranges components, builds cars and supplies dealers or export buyers. For example, a household may choose a family car at a dealership. The manufacturer builds and supplies it; the dealer handles the customer sale under its arrangement. Later parts and service needs are related work, but separate purchases.
money: The company receives payment for vehicles, parts and related goods or services. It pays for components, workers, factories, transport, developing models, advertising and promised repairs. The difference between a car’s showroom price and its material cost is not all manufacturer profit.
customers: Dealers and export buyers that receive cars from the manufacturer, and people or businesses eventually buying those vehicles. A dealer buying a car and a driver registering it are different stages.
drivers: How many cars buyers want, which models they choose, discounts, loan affordability, component costs, factory output and the cost of developing future vehicles.

groups.title: Passenger vehicles
groups.examples: Swift, Dzire, WagonR, Ertiga and other models.
groups.explanation: These carry people for different needs and budgets. A small hatchback, a sedan with a separate boot and a larger family vehicle have different features, prices and costs.

groups.title: Routes to buyers
groups.examples: ARENA, NEXA and commercial or institutional sales routes.
groups.explanation: These are ways of reaching customers, not separate car manufacturers. Their names do not by themselves identify separate reported profits.

groups.title: Keeping a vehicle in use
groups.examples: Genuine parts, accessories, authorised service and related programmes.
groups.explanation: Owners need parts, maintenance and repairs after buying a car. Dealers and partners can carry out some of that work; not every payment made at a service outlet belongs to the manufacturer.

groups.title: Used-car channels and exports
groups.examples: True Value used-car activity and new vehicles supplied overseas.
groups.explanation: Helping sell a used car is different from manufacturing a new one. Overseas buyers also face different prices, currencies and delivery arrangements from Indian buyers.

basics.title: A car sent to a dealer is not yet the same as a car bought by a driver
basics.text: Dispatches are vehicles sent into the sales chain. Retail sales or registrations describe a later stage. Dealers can build up unsold stock, so compare the measures rather than treating them as interchangeable.

steps.title: Plan the model and obtain components
steps.text: Arrange designs, technology, parts and suppliers for the kind of vehicle buyers need.

steps.title: Build and check the car
steps.text: Factories assemble and test vehicles. Missing components, faults or production delays can interrupt this work.

steps.title: Supply a dealer or overseas buyer
steps.text: Send cars under the agreed sales and payment terms. The manufacturer’s sale and the driver’s final purchase need not happen together.

steps.title: Collect payment and support the product
steps.text: Payments must cover making and selling the vehicle and other business costs. Parts, repairs and promised fault-related support continue after the initial sale.

specifics.title: Different cars change the sales value
specifics.text: More buyers choosing larger or better-equipped cars can raise revenue even without a similar increase in cars sold. Extra features can also cost more to provide.

specifics.title: The buyer must afford more than the car’s price
specifics.text: Loan interest, eligibility for credit, fuel, maintenance, taxes and the value of a traded-in car can affect the decision to buy.

specifics.title: New engines, electric systems and factories need paying buyers
specifics.text: Gas-powered CNG vehicles, hybrids that combine an engine with electric assistance, and battery-electric vehicles need different technology and supporting facilities. Money spent developing a vehicle or factory comes before proof that enough buyers will cover its costs.

watch: Are dealers selling the cars they receive?
Unsold dealer stock can grow before driver demand does.
Compare manufacturer dispatches with retail-sales and stock commentary for the same period. Festivals and delivery dates can shift purchases between months.
Do higher-priced cars leave more after costs?
Extra features and discounts can absorb a higher selling price.
Read model choices, discounts and component costs together. A model’s price list does not disclose its profit.
Can factories and suppliers meet real demand?
Both shortages and idle equipment can be costly.
Follow production, parts availability, new-factory progress and orders. A waiting list can reflect limited supply, and buyers can cancel.
How do exports and exchange rates affect the result?
Foreign sales and imported parts involve different currencies.
Read export quantities, overseas demand and currency explanations. A rupee conversion change is not the same thing as more cars wanted by customers.
How much cash do future cars and promised repairs require?
Development and repair obligations can cost money after a strong sales year.

Read spending on models and equipment, day-to-day cash generation, warranty provisions and recalls. A warranty provision is money set aside in the accounts for expected repair obligations. Keep Maruti India separate from other Suzuki businesses.
risks: Weaker incomes or more expensive loans can delay a large purchase.
Parts or quality problems stop work
Component shortages and faults can interrupt production, require recalls or damage confidence.
A new range fails to attract enough buyers
Changing technology and competing models can make investment hard to recover.
Materials, currency movements and safety or emissions requirements can raise the cost of a vehicle.
context: A booking is an earlier stage than a completed sale

An enquiry, a booking, a car sent to a dealer and a driver taking it home are different events. Read when the company records its sale and whether vehicles are waiting in the dealer chain before treating popularity as earned profit.
quiz: If revenue rises faster than the number of cars sold, did customer demand necessarily rise equally?
No. Different models, prices, exports and related services can change the sales value. Check quantities and costs too.

financialNotes.title: The model list is not a profit split
financialNotes.text: The table shows audited consolidated revenue from operations and profit after tax. Revenue includes products, services and other operating revenue, and differs from a standalone net-sales headline. A model’s retail price, bookings or factory capacity cannot be used to invent its manufacturer revenue or profit.
